comments.note: TaggerView.axaml uses x:Name='Root' on the UserControl root element to enable named-element binding from within nested DataTemplates (e.g. ContextMenu inside item template). This is a valid Avalonia pattern but slightly unusual. If Avalonia removes named-root NameScope resolution in a future version, the ContextMenu command bindings would silently fail at runtime. An alternative is a code-behind ContextMenu.Opening handler that sets commands imperatively.

DepthToMarginConverter.cs is a new converter in Converters/ (src/VideoIndexer.App/Converters/DepthToMarginConverter.cs). The Instance singleton is defined but TaggerView.axaml uses a resource key declaration instead — both patterns exist in the project (IntDecimalConverter uses both). No inconsistency in practice, but a style guide clarification on preferred usage would prevent future duplication.

TaggerViewModel.SelectedCategory and TaggerViewModel.SelectedTag are bidirectionally bound from TaggerView but TaggerViewModel never consumes them in any command logic — they appear to be placeholders for future right-click selection state used by context-menu enablement (CanExecute). Until a CanExecute guard is added to EditTagCommand/DeleteTagCommand/MergeTagCommand, those commands are always enabled regardless of whether an item is selected. This is consistent with the current TaggerViewModel implementation (no CanExecute guards), so no action is needed in this WP.

comments.note: ContextMenu bindings use {Binding #Root.((vm:TaggerViewModel)DataContext).EditTagCommand} / DeleteTagCommand / MergeTagCommand. ContextMenu is a Popup placed in a separate visual overlay tree in Avalonia; named-element resolution for #Root may silently fail at runtime because the ContextMenu NameScope does not include names from the parent UserControl. Compiled binding resolved statically without errors, but runtime correctness is not covered by any unit or headless UI test. This is flagged by the developer in handoff notes. Recommend adding a headless smoke test or runtime assertion in a future WP to confirm context menu commands fire.

SelectedItem on the ListBox inside TabControl.ContentTemplate binds via element cast: {Binding #Root.((vm:TaggerViewModel)DataContext).SelectedTag}. Since ContentTemplate is within a separate DataTemplate scope with x:DataType='vm:TaggerCategoryViewModel', the element-reference cast to TaggerViewModel must succeed at runtime. Compiled binding accepts this statically; runtime verification pending integration with an actual TaggerViewModel instance.

No unit or headless UI test for TaggerView itself was added in this WP (TaggerView is purely an AXAML view scaffold). The WP scope does not require tests, but for full regression coverage a headless UI test confirming ViewLocator resolution and basic binding attachment would be valuable in a subsequent WP.

ContextMenu #Root named-element binding assessed: In Avalonia 11, compiled element-name bindings are resolved at AXAML compile-time via code generation, not at visual-tree traversal time. ContextMenu items maintain a logical parent reference back to the host UserControl, so FindNameScope resolves #Root through the logical tree. The 0-warning clean build from the Avalonia AXAML compiler confirms the generated binding code is valid. Not a blocking concern.
DepthToMarginConverter.Instance property mirrors the IntDecimalConverter precedent already in the project — intentional, not dead code.
Inline Grid.Styles inside the DataTemplate is intentional (co-location with usage, more discoverable). No Fix-Forward applied.

DepthToMarginConverter.Instance static property is declared but not used in any AXAML file (TaggerView uses the StaticResource key). This mirrors the IntDecimalConverter precedent in the project, where Instance is similarly declared but all views use StaticResource. The pattern is intentional. A style guide note clarifying when to prefer {x:Static Instance} vs {StaticResource Key} would help future contributors.

[documentation-forward] TaggerViewModel has a known unmanaged subscription: it subscribes to ITagsManager.DataChanged in the constructor but never unsubscribes. The class docstring correctly warns callers to unsubscribe when the Tagger is no longer visible. The api-surface.md and constraints.md should document this lifecycle contract explicitly — callers (future WPs that instantiate TaggerViewModel) must call ITagsManager.DataChanged -= handler on disposal, ideally by having TaggerViewModel implement IDisposable in a future WP.
